children: Australian 10-year government bond yields have been drifting lower as traders question the artificial intelligence trade, says Jack Chambers, debt strategist at ANZ. Fed speakers have also appeared more cautious about further hikes, he adds. Still, this could be only a temporary reprieve as over time these factors will reverse, he says. ANZ expects the Reserve Bank of Australia and Fed will both hike at their next meetings and it seems pre-emptive to call time on the AI trade, Chambers adds. Aussie bond yields will likely be higher by the end of the year, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
